GameLobby.title: GameLobby
GameLobby.description: Represents a game lobby where players can join before starting a game.

id.description: Unique identifier for the GameLobby entity.

accessCode.description: Short code used for players to join the lobby.

creatorId.description: Reference to the User who created the lobby. (Relationship: User 1:N GameLobby)

playerIds.description: References to Users currently in the lobby. (Relationship: User N:N GameLobby)

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the lobby was created.

status.description: The status of the game lobby

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

googleId.description: Google identifier for users who signed up using Google Auth.

username.description: The display name of the user.

email.description: The email address of the user.

Game.title: Game
Game.description: Represents an instance of a game being played.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Game entity.

lobbyId.description: Reference to the GameLobby this game belongs to. (Relationship: GameLobby 1:1 Game)

playerIds.description: References to Users participating in this game. (Relationship: User N:N Game)

currentRound.description: The current round number of the game.

status.description: The current status of the game (e.g., LOBBY, BETTING, PLAYING, SCORING).

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the game was created.

firestore.reasoning:
This design prioritizes authorization independence and secure list operations (QAPs). It leverages path-based ownership for user-specific data (GameLobbies) and denormalization of authorization data within game lobbies and games themselves. The structure is segregated to ensure homogeneous security requirements for each collection.

1.  **Authorization Independence:** The `GameLobby` includes the `creatorId` and `playerIds`, effectively denormalizing the authorization context. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in security rules to check the parent user's ownership, enabling atomic operations.

2.  **Secure List Operations (QAPs):**  The `GameLobbies` are created as subcollections of `/users/{userId}`. This inherently limits listing to a user's own lobbies (or requires admin privileges). The games created inside a given lobby also inherit the authorization context (via denormalized `playerIds`) and limit `list` access.

3.  **DBAC (Database-Based Access Control):** No custom claims are used. Authorization relies solely on `request.auth.uid` and the data stored in Firestore.

4.  **Structural Segregation:**  All `GameLobby` documents in a given collection share the same security requirements, simplifying rules.

5.  **Access Modeling:** User-owned `GameLobby` entities are structured using hierarchical paths (`/users/{userId}/gameLobbies/{gameLobbyId}`). This pattern ensures clear ownership and simplifies security rules based on path matching.

6. **Radical Consistency:** The naming conventions used are consistent (e.g., `creatorId`, `playerIds`).
